title: SCE test log (wire schema v1)
description: The test log of one run of one test case of the test profile (docs/adr/0091 C3 and answer 8; docs/SCE_TEST_PROFILE.md section 12.5): the test verdict and the records of TCI's test logging interface (ETSI ES 201 873-6), each written where the profile's semantics places its event, in the order the round scheduler produces them. Both runtimes of a suite write it, the native one and the TTCN-3 one, and a run of the same suite against the same input trace must give the same log on both sides; a disagreement is the test case's error. The text is the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785) of the log, and the log holds no number: an instant, a duration and every integer of a value are the text of their decimal digits, since a 64-bit integer is past what a reader that holds numbers as doubles reads exactly. Two logs therefore agree exactly when their bytes do. A message carries the name of its record type as the export's types module names it, and its value in the canonical form of the profile's types: an integer the text of its digits, a bool a truth value, a value of an enum the name its document declares, a text a text, a byte string its octets in upper-case hex, a record an object of its fields by their declared ids with an absent field omitted, a list an array, and a value of a union an object of one member, its case's variant, whose value is the case's record or the empty object. Authoritative producer is backends/rust/runtime/src/test/test_log.rs over the runs of backends/rust/runtime/src/test/run.rs. The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone; see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md for the shared policy.

schema.description: The name of this shape. Changed only on a breaking shape change.

suite.description: The name of the test suite the test case was run in.

test_case.description: The name of the test case.

records.description: The records of the run, in the order the round scheduler produced them. The first is the test case's start and the last its end.

verdict.description: A test verdict, spelled as TTCN-3 spells it.

count.description: A whole number of microseconds, at least 0, as the text of its decimal digits.

name.description: The name of a component (`mtc` or a PTC's name in its configuration), a component type, a port or a timer.

value.description: A value in the canonical form of the profile's types: a text, a truth value, an array of values, or an object of values. Never a number and never null.

record.description: One record: `at`, NOW when it was written, `kind`, the TCI event in kebab case, and the members of its kind.

test-case-started.description: The test case started, at NOW 0 (P11).

test-case-ended.description: The test case ended with its verdict (P14).

component-created.description: A component was created: the MTC as the test case starts, a PTC when the invocation that creates it starts (P9).

component-done.description: A component terminated, with its local verdict then (P10).

message-type.description: The name of a message's record type as the types module of the suite's TTCN-3 export names it (docs/SCE_TEST_PROFILE.md section 9.5): the unit name of its event-schema document. A value in TCI always carries its type, so a message of the log does too.

message-sent.description: A component sent a message on one of its ports (P6).

message-received.description: A receive branch took the head of a port's queue: the message was received and matched (P4).

timer-started.description: A component started a timer for a duration in microseconds (P7).

timer-stopped.description: A component stopped a running timer (P7). The stop of a timer that is not running changes nothing and is not recorded.

timer-timed-out.description: A timeout branch took a timer that had timed out (P4).

verdict-set.description: A component's local verdict was set, by the document (P12) or to error by the runtime (P13). The reason is the document's, omitted where it gave none; the runtime's error carries none.
